title: Drop the mid-depth global layer: WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL" -> "SSSS"
description: One character in the hyperparameter block: WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL" -> "SSSS", so layer 3 goes from window 2048 to 512 and only the forced-long last layer keeps full context (7x512 + 1x2048). val_bpb 0.990153 vs the control pair's 0.989825 (n=2 at 6x512+2x2048) - a small raw LOSS, because FLOPs/token fell 4.3% but MFU fell 35.89% -> 33.73% and tokens fell 486.4M -> 477.9M.
reflection:
Two findings, and the throughput one is the more useful.

1. NEGATIVE, mildly: raw val_bpb 0.990153 against the control mean 0.989825 (a2's two byte-identical SSSL/512 runs, 0.989668 and 0.989981, spread 0.0003), i.e. +0.00033. Not a win; do not carry this forward on its own.

2. THE FLOP MODEL IS BROKEN ON THIS AXIS AND EVERYONE IS BUDGETING WITH IT. estimate_flops fell 220.2M -> 210.8M per token (-4.3%), and tokens went DOWN, 486.4M -> 477.9M (-1.7%), because steady-state MFU fell 35.89% -> 33.73%. Converting one full-2048 layer into a 512-window layer costs more in FA3 kernel efficiency than the arithmetic it saves. The MFU series across the whole window sweep is monotone in how much windowing we do: 37.8% (6x1024+2x2048, 469.5M tok) -> 35.9% (6x512+2x2048, 486.4M) -> 33.7% (7x512+1x2048, 477.9M). Tokens peaked at the middle config, which is the current baseline. a2 already flagged in #64 that the 1024->512 cut returned only a third of its predicted tokens; this run shows the next notch returns NEGATIVE tokens. Any further 'cut attention FLOPs to buy tokens' argument should be considered refuted until someone measures otherwise.

3. Token-corrected, the quality direction is still mildly favourable: at 477.9M the token model (slope -0.000128/1M off the control) predicts 0.990913; I measured 0.990153, a residual of -0.00076, about 1.3 sd. So deleting the mid-depth global layer is roughly quality-neutral-to-slightly-good PER TOKEN and loses only on throughput. Read together with a2's -0.0020 residual at 1024->512, the picture is that cross-document span is mildly harmful to quality but we have run out of ways to convert that into wall-clock, because the kernel gets less efficient exactly as fast as the FLOPs come down.

4. Prediction for the sibling runs this round, on the record before I see them: a1's all-short (8x512, both global layers deleted) should lose more on MFU than mine and land near or above 0.990; a2's 6x256+2x2048 should show the same kernel tax at an even smaller block size. If both come in flat-to-worse, the attention-span axis is closed at the current baseline and the remaining 12-ish runs should go somewhere else entirely - and NOT into another scalar LR, which rounds 2 measured flat below 0.04 and cliff-edged above.
